root_cause_finding.summary: The 2 phenomena originally described as separate ('2 empty Wikisource positions behind 2:8/36:35' and '2 unresolved real-text segments at S2 ordinal 287 / S36 ordinal 84') are symptoms of ONE single upstream extraction bug, not independent anomalies and not a coincidence inferred merely because both counts were 2.
root_cause_finding.mechanism: texte_entier_raw.html contains exactly 2 genuinely empty <li class="mw-empty-elt"> elements inside a surah's <ol> (Surah 2, physically right after real item 6; Surah 36, physically right after real item 34) -- confirmed by direct grep/parse of the frozen HTML, not a prior summary. Phase 3's extractor (kazimirski_html_extract.py, function extract_li_items) split on every <li> tag and appended ALL of them, including these 2 empty ones, to its per-surah items list, then enumerated that list 1..N to assign source_ordinal. This gave the empty <li> a real position slot (Surah 2 slot 7; Surah 36 slot 35), so every REAL item after it was numbered exactly one too high for the rest of the surah. generate_manifest.py then looked up each item's canonical target by indexing into segment_classification_full.csv's declared_num sequence using this now-off-by-one source_ordinal, producing a systematic +1 target mismatch for every segment after the gap in both surahs. Phase 1's original CSV-population process had independently fallen into the identical trap (its own french_text column is also off-by-one for Surah 2 items 7-286 and Surah 36 items 35-83), which is why the mis-map was not caught by the existing fresh-vs-CSV sanity cross-check in generate_manifest.py -- both sides agreed on the same wrong answer.
root_cause_finding.critical_clarification: The empty <li> elements do NOT correspond to any missing verse. Every canonical ayah in both surahs already has real, complete Kazimirski French text present in the frozen source. Task 1's original framing ('is text recoverable from the 1869 scan') turned out to have a different true answer than expected: no text needed recovery from any external scan -- the text was always present in texte_entier_raw.html, just joined to the wrong ayah number.
primary_source_evidence:
Direct grep of texte_entier_raw.html confirms exactly 3 occurrences of the string 'mw-empty-elt' in the whole 2,137,011-byte document: 1 unrelated

before Surah 1's heading (front matter, not inside any surah's

    ), and 2 real
  1. elements, one in Surah 2's
      (offset ~151115, immediately after the item ending '...le châtiment cruel les attend.'), one in Surah 36's
        (offset ~1059003, immediately after the item ending '...nous y avons fait jaillir des sources,').

Actual 1869 Charpentier page-scan image retrieved directly (Wikisource djvu page images for Le_Koran_(traduction_de_Kazimirski).djvu pages 3 and 358, same provenance chain as Google Books ID 3XSe413MJyQC per PHASE1-ALIGNMENT-AUDIT.md). Page 3 shows Kazimirski's own printed verse numbers running continuously 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11... with NO gap and no missing content at the point corresponding to the empty <li>; verse '7' on the printed page reads 'Il est des hommes qui disent : Nous croyons en Dieu et au jour dernier ; et cependant ils ne sont pas du nombre des croyants.' -- present, complete, and correctly typeset.

Independent cross-check against the local governed Pickthall English translation (content_sources.id=6d6c4315-e426-4671-840b-0d25b31a683e, same canonical Cairo numbering as `ayahs`) at more than 15 points spanning each surah from its start to its final ayah (2:7-2:12, 2:154-2:155, 2:203-2:204, 2:282-2:286 for Surah 2; 36:32-36:41, 36:81-36:83 for Surah 36), all confirming the corrected mapping and refuting the DB's pre-Phase-4 mapping at every one of those points.

Exhaustive structural reconciliation: applying the correction (re-index by excluding the empty <li> from the physical position count, then re-look-up each item's canonical target via segment_classification_full.csv's already-Flügel/Cairo-difflib-derived classification) to all 286 Surah 2 segments and all 83 Surah 36 segments produces EXACT, gapless, non-overlapping coverage of canonical 2:1-2:286 and 36:1-36:83, with split/merge event counts (Surah 2: 9 one_to_many, 18 many_to_one items forming 9 two-way merges; Surah 36: 1 one_to_many, 2 many_to_one items forming 1 two-way merge) matching PHASE1-ALIGNMENT-AUDIT.md's own independently-computed A/B/C/D matrix counts for these two surahs exactly (Surah 2: A=22,B=237,C=9,D=18; Surah 36: A=52,B=28,C=1,D=2).

changes.old_state: extract_li_items() appended every <li> element's cleaned text to its items list, including genuinely empty ones, giving them a permanent ordinal slot. generate_manifest.py's EXTRA-1 handling treated the resulting trailing item in Surah 2/36 as a genuine extra unresolved physical segment (source_ordinal 287/84), and its fresh-vs-CSV sanity cross-check assumed CSV text was reliable for classification purposes past the gap.
changes.new_state: extract_li_items() now skips any <li> whose cleaned text is empty/whitespace-only when building the items list, so it never consumes a position slot (no text was added, removed, or altered by this change -- it only affects which physical position each REAL item's already-existing text is assigned to). generate_manifest.py's EXTRA-1 handling now asserts the gap is closed (fresh_list length == declared count) rather than emitting an unresolved segment; the sanity cross-check has a narrowly-scoped, documented exception for the known Phase-1-CSV text-cache shift range in Surah 2 (items >=7) and Surah 36 (items >=35), where canonical_ayah_range (not text) is trusted from the CSV. CROSS_VERIFIED_ITEMS was updated to mark all of Surah 2 and Surah 36 as Phase-4-verified ('ALL').
changes.reason: Fixes the bug at its source so future manifest regenerations are correct without needing this patch re-applied by hand, and produces a manifest whose aggregate_ordered_hash and per-segment text_sha256 values are byte-identical to before (verified: aggregate_ordered_hash unchanged, all 6239 non-preamble segments' text_sha256 match the pre-existing DB rows exactly).
